transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Um, yeah… I guess the main thing is I get pulled off track really easily. Like I’ll be working on a dashboard I’m supposed to finish, and then one Slack ping comes in, or even just a song lyric gets stuck in my head, or I suddenly think of a totally different project, and then I’ve completely lost the thread. It’s frustrating because I know what I’m supposed to be doing, but it’s like my brain just… wanders off.
Can you tell me how far back these attention and focus difficulties go—did you notice them as far back as childhood, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, it goes pretty far back. Like elementary school, definitely. I remember — well, I don’t remember all of it, but my parents still have some of my old report cards somewhere, in this folder my mom keeps with, like, every certificate I ever got, which is kind of embarrassing.

But the comments were always things like I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow the directions all the way, or I’d lose track of what we were supposed to be doing. And during group work I guess I’d talk over people a lot. At home, my parents used to literally sit next to me while I did homework because if they didn’t, I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished. So… yeah, it’s not really new.
Aside from the attention difficulties, do you notice things like feeling restless, needing to move around a lot, fidgeting, or acting or speaking impulsively before thinking things through?

Yeah, I think so. Like, if I’m stuck sitting through a long Zoom call or I’m supposed to just quietly work in one spot, I get this… uncomfortable kind of pressure in my body? Like I need to get up or pace around or at least do something with my hands.

It’s not always dramatic or anything, but it’s there. I’ll be sitting there trying to pay attention, and then I’m thinking about how badly I want to stand up, or I start messing with whatever’s near me—like a pen or my water bottle. Zoom calls are the worst for it, honestly.
Do you often find yourself interrupting or finishing other people's sentences, blurting out answers before a question is fully asked, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yeah… mostly in conversations where people are brainstorming. I’ll get excited because I can see the idea in my head, and I’ll just kind of jump in before they’re done explaining it.

Like if we’re working on a Figma board, I might start adding my idea or moving things around while someone is still talking, and then afterward I’m like, oh… that probably came off really pushy. I don’t mean it that way, I’m just trying to help or I’m excited, but I can tell it doesn’t always land well.
Would you say these attention and impulsivity issues have caused real problems for you in more than one area of your life—like at work, in your relationships, or with day-to-day responsibilities?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life is falling apart, because it’s not, but it has caused actual problems.

Like with freelance stuff — small design things, not huge jobs or anything — I’ve lost a couple contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly, or I’d miss some detail and then people felt like they couldn’t count on me. And there was this portfolio competition I really wanted to enter, and I had all these ideas for it, I even made this messy inspiration board with colors and references and— sorry, that’s not really the point. I ended up missing out because I couldn’t get it together in time.

And socially, too, with friends or collaborators. People like my ideas, I think, but some of them are hesitant to work with me because they’re not sure I’ll actually finish things the way I say I will. That feels… pretty bad, honestly.
